newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO submits findings on 1980 plane crash.
newsitem.headline: NATO submits findings on 1980 plane crash.

text.p: NATO said on Friday it had sent fresh information to the Italian judge investigating an air crash near the Mediterranean island of Ustica in 1980 which the Italian media have long speculated was caused by a NATO missile.
NATO said in a statement it had sent its analysis of a computer tape from the day of the incident, when 81 people died but gave no details of its findings.

"At the request of the Italian authorities, NATO technical experts have analysed and interpreted the contents of this computer tape and have provided their findings to Judge (Rosario) Priore over the last two days," it said.
"This analysis involved considerable effort, the development of a great deal of new software and was completed in less than one month."

It said the findings were submitted after a two-day meeting starting on December 18 of a special committee -- consisting of three NATO experts, one legal, one security and one military, set up to investigate the matter.
Italy has frequently called on NATO to release secret radar charts relating to the crash of the Itavia domestic airline DC-9 near Ustica, some 40 miles (60 km) north of Sicily on June 27, 1980.
